newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent weaker Monday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, dealers said.
Follow-through selling from Friday's close near the lows could pressure the benchmark July contract to support at 72.00 cents a lb, followed by 70.00 cents, they said.
Friday, July cotton settled 0.73 cent lower at 72.37 cents after trading from 73.20 to 73.16 cents. New-crop December went out 0.57 cent lower at 75.05 cents.
An estimated 14,000 lots changed hands on the day.

CFTC's Commitments of Traders Report released after the close Friday showed the speculators to be holding a net short position of about 17 percent as of May 27. Analysts said that number has probably declined to between 12-15 percent, and is not likely to nudge prices out of their recent range.
In fundamental news, cool wet weather throughout much of the cotton belt continues to keep crop development behind schedule, Weather Services Corp, said. Planting is nearly complete in many areas.
USDA will issue its weekly crop progress report at 1600 EDT.
